name: Four Seasons Hotel at the Surf Club
insider_take: Where golden-age Hollywood glamour meets modern Four Seasons luxury on one of Miami Beach's most storied stretches of sand.
whats_special: The Four Seasons at the Surf Club isn't just a hotel — it's a resurrection of legend. The original Surf Club, founded in 1930, was once the most exclusive private club in America, hosting icons like Frank Sinatra, Elizabeth Taylor, and Winston Churchill. Today, architect Richard Meier's stunning towers rise alongside the meticulously restored 1930s historic clubhouse, blending Art Deco heritage with contemporary elegance. The result is an oceanfront masterpiece on Surfside's quiet, uncrowded shores — just north of South Beach's buzz, yet worlds apart in serenity.
pro_tip: Request a suite in the historic Surf Club building itself for an unmatched sense of place — the restored ballroom and Tower Bar are worth a visit even if you're staying in the modern towers.
dont_miss: Dinner at Le Sirenuse Miami , the acclaimed outpost of the legendary Positano restaurant, serving refined Southern Italian cuisine with an ocean view. Then unwind at the sprawling spa, one of the largest in Miami, or simply stake your claim on the pristine private beach — where the Atlantic feels like it was made just for you.
pros: Historic Art Deco architecture blended with modern luxury design
Exclusive oceanfront location with private beach access
Multiple world-class dining venues including Le Sirenuse Miami
Exceptional spa and wellness facilities with ocean views
Legendary Four Seasons service and attention to detail
cons: Ultra-luxury pricing reflective of exclusive positioning
Limited availability due to high demand and exclusivity
